Edit: I'm around 40h in and still hooked on the game. The powers mechanic really makes you feel you have a hand in how each run will flow - and you're open to make any build that suits you like focusing on frost-type or fire-type attacks, vitality scaling damage or other things like that. It also has an ever-improving detailed stats breakdown window which can help you see which pet, passive or any source of status is contributing by whichever amount to your current run. There's A LOT of game modes and almost all of them provide permanent bonuses for your account and future runs. This along the prestige system works very well to the incremental part here and keeps you engaged in "just another run" for hours on end till its 3am. The dev replies very quickly to the players questions both on the discussions forum on steam and on the newly created discord, actively engaging with me and other players and patching bugs + doing QoL improvements, which is amazing. I also like the global leaderboard and it seems we're going to get a PVP/arena mode soon, with some neat features like friends and rivals to compare and spar. I suggest joining the discord if you like it to learn a bit more, as the plethora of info can be a bit confusing or misleading at times, but the little community being formed here seems pretty friendly for now (dev is constantly changing and working to improve the in-game compendium and the tooltip/description of everything whenever we mention it with him). The price is considered low as well. All in all, solid thumbs up if you like idler/incremental games.

Overall i'm enjoying this game. The basic gameplay loop works well and while the prestige system felt a little slow at first (as always in idle games) it sped up pretty quickly. I haven't really gotten into the alternate modes / mini games too much yet, but the bits I have played seemed like decent changes of pace, though, im not sure I get how the powers actually work in the labyrinth. Ill likely keep fiddling with this for a good long while as i try to find the cheesiest power buildouts. There is a high degree of control of the automation systems so that you can automate only the things you want to while still manually selecting the more important stuff (like power choices) which is nice.

Had this one wish listed and snagged it right when it released. I've played basically every idle game worth playing and this one is really satisfying The prestige layer actually means something here, you're thinking about resetting pretty quick, which is exactly what you want. There's also an optimization puzzle underneath if you want to dig in, but it plays well passively too. Offline progress is fair and doesn't feel punishing. Huge deal. - I'm enjoying popping in to check on things here and there between my other projects. [b]If you know you love the genre, just buy it. If you've bounced off idle games before, this is a good one to retry.[/b] Recommended

I love the depth and complexity of the game. My biggest problem is not letting it 'idle'... I want to keep tweaking the knobs to see if I can improve my run. I've barely scratched the surface on all the play modes and truly can't put it down.

Idle Regenerator has serious addictive potential and is already a strong contender for one of the best idle games of 2026. The game has a great progression loop, plenty of things to do, and a surprising amount of build variety thanks to its different powers. Trying out new combinations and optimizing your runs is a lot of fun, and the leaderboard adds an extra layer of motivation for those who enjoy pushing for better results. Pros: Nice graphics and presentation Lots of content and progression systems High replay value thanks to different powers and builds Many ways to gain passive bonuses and long-term progression Leaderboards encourage optimization and competition Prestige automation has many useful options and features Cons: Prestige should have a player-defined goal, for example: "Prestige at X PP points." If combat continues while you're choosing a new power, another power selection window can appear and you end up losing one of your power choices for that run.

Incredibly Addictive – Highly Recommended! Pros: Tons of Content: There are so many things to unlock, which keeps the game feeling rewarding for a long time. Great Features: The leaderboard, active events, and achievements add fantastic replay value. Awesome Developer: The developer is deeply committed to the game and responds incredibly fast to feedback. The Only Downside: The only thing that bothers me at the moment is that the Labyrinth Mode lacks a full automation option. I would really love to see this part of the game become fully "idle" in a future update. Verdict: Other than that, it's a fantastic game! Check it out, I highly recommend it.

It's an idle game, that has so many things running at once, all of which don't really do anything. Nothing interconnects through the game, its like 6 idle games in one. Except not one of them is interesting. It feels silly to say an idle game doesn't respect your time, but the siege turtle thing was an idle game that took forever to get going, but every time your run finished you had important and useful upgrades. This game auto prestiges you because it truly doesn't matter. Your numbers go up, and there is no story. Also its locked in a web page, so you can right click and close the game in your mindless clicking in the first bit when gameplay matters. The ui is trash, and can't improve because its a webpage.
